articles.title: What's Left to Build When Software Is Free (with Chip Huyen)
articles.description:
#AIengineering #MachineLearning #FoundationModels 

Chip Huyen joins host @JonKrohnLearns for this milestone episode 999 to talk about her record-breaking book "AI Engineering" the most-read title on the O'Reilly platform last year and how the AI landscape has shifted since her last appearance. Chip breaks down what separates AI engineering from machine learning engineering, makes the case for a "start simple" workflow, gets candid about the real costs of running LLMs in production, and shares why she's now fascinated by physical AI, robotics, and world models and why the durable problems worth solving are increasingly human ones. Jon Krohn guides the conversation from the practical content of the book through to where the field is heading next.

This episode is brought to you by: 
• Cisco: https://outshift.cisco.com
• Acceldata: https://www.acceldata.io

Interested in sponsoring a SuperDataScience Podcast episode? Email natalie@superdatascience.com for sponsorship information.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:06:48) What separates AI engineering from machine learning engineering
• (00:14:44) The “start simple” approach: prompting, then RAG, then fine-tuning
• (00:18:19) Why web search is so painfully expensive in production
• (00:35:21) Is the “ChatGPT moment” for physical AI really here?
• (00:53:08) Why the durable problems left to solve are people problems

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/999

articles.title: Agile Robots: Building VLAs and World Models
articles.description: In this episode, I sit down at the Agile Robots headquarters in Munich with Laurenz von Czettritz to dive deep into the evolving world of robotics and AI. We explore why NVIDIA’s frameworks dominate the industry, what it really takes to build new physical AI solutions, and how foundation models are reshaping automation. Laurenz shares how his team is developing next-generation AI for robotics, from building their own models to tackling unique industrial data challenges. We discuss the obstacles, breakthroughs, and the strategic mindset required to stay ahead in this rapidly changing field. If you’re curious about the real-world journey to smarter, more adaptable robots, this conversation offers a candid look inside the industry’s most ambitious projects.
